True Statement: Growth can be defined as an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ or its parts or even of an individual cell.
False 1: Growth can be defined as a reversible permanent increase in size of an organ or its parts or even of an individual cell.

True Statement: Growth is accompanied by metabolic processes (both anabolic and catabolic) that occur at the expense of energy.
False 1: Growth is accompanied by metabolic processes (both anabolic and catabolic) that produce energy rather than occurring at its expense.

True Statement: Plant growth is unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life.
False 1: Plant growth is unique because plants lose the capacity for growth after reaching maturity.

True Statement: The ability of plants to grow throughout their life is due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body.
False 1: The ability of plants to grow throughout their life is due to the presence of parenchyma at certain locations in their body.

True Statement: The cells of meristems have the capacity to divide and self-perpetuate.
False 1: The cells of meristems have lost the capacity to divide and self-perpetuate.

True Statement: The form of growth wherein new cells are always being added to the plant body by the activity of the meristem is called the open form of growth.
False 1: The form of growth wherein new cells are always being added to the plant body by the activity of the meristem is called the closed form of growth.

True Statement: Root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem are responsible for the primary growth of plants and principally contribute to the elongation of the plants along their axis.
False 1: Lateral meristems (vascular cambium and cork-cambium) are responsible for the primary growth of plants.
False 2: Root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem are responsible for the secondary growth of plants and principally contribute to the elongation of the plants along their axis.

True Statement: In dicotyledonous plants and gymnosperms, the lateral meristems – vascular cambium and cork-cambium – appear later in life.
False 1: In monocotyledonous plants and gymnosperms, the lateral meristems – vascular cambium and cork-cambium – appear later in life.

True Statement: Vascular cambium and cork-cambium cause the increase in the girth of the organs in which they are active; this is known as secondary growth.
False 1: Root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem cause the increase in the girth of the organs in which they are active; this is known as secondary growth.

True Statement: Growth at a cellular level is principally a consequence of increase in the amount of protoplasm.
False 1: Growth at a cellular level is principally a consequence of increase in the amount of cell wall material.

True Statement: One single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour.
False 1: One single watermelon root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour.

True Statement: Cells in a watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times.
False 1: Cells in a maize root apical meristem may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times.

True Statement: The period of growth is generally divided into three phases: meristematic, elongation and maturation.
False 1: The period of growth is generally divided into two phases: meristematic and elongation.

True Statement: Cells in the meristematic phase are rich in protoplasm and possess large conspicuous nuclei.
False 1: Cells in the maturation phase are rich in protoplasm and possess large conspicuous nuclei.

True Statement: Cell walls in the meristematic phase are primary in nature, thin and cellulosic with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.
False 1: Cell walls in the meristematic phase are secondary in nature, thick and lignocellulosic.

True Statement: Cells in the elongation phase show increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition.
False 1: Cells in the meristematic phase show increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition.

True Statement: Cells in the maturation phase attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.
False 1: Cells in the elongation phase attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.

True Statement: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures.
False 1: In geometric growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures.

True Statement: Arithmetic growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate.
False 1: Geometric growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate.

True Statement: In arithmetic growth, plotting the length of the organ against time gives a linear curve.
False 1: In geometric growth, plotting the length of the organ against time gives a linear curve.
False 2: In arithmetic growth, plotting the length of the organ against time gives a sigmoid curve.

True Statement: In geometric growth, both progeny cells following mitotic cell division retain the ability to divide.
False 1: In arithmetic growth, both progeny cells following mitotic cell division retain the ability to divide.

True Statement: A sigmoid curve is a characteristic of living organisms growing in a natural environment.
False 1: A linear curve is a characteristic of living organisms growing in a natural environment.

True Statement: In geometric growth, the initial growth is slow (lag phase) and it increases rapidly thereafter at an exponential rate (log phase).
False 1: In geometric growth, the initial growth is rapid (log phase) and it slows down thereafter.

True Statement: Measurement and comparison of total growth per unit time is called the absolute growth rate.
False 1: Measurement and comparison of total growth per unit time is called the relative growth rate.

True Statement: The growth of a given system per unit time expressed per unit initial parameter is called the relative growth rate.
False 1: The growth of a given system per unit time expressed per unit initial parameter is called the absolute growth rate.

True Statement: Plant cells grow in size by cell enlargement which requires water.
False 1: Plant cells grow in size by cell division alone, which requires water.

True Statement: Turgidity of cells helps in extension growth.
False 1: Loss of turgidity of cells helps in extension growth.

True Statement: Oxygen helps in releasing metabolic energy essential for growth activities.
False 1: Carbon dioxide helps in releasing metabolic energy essential for growth activities.

True Statement: The act leading to maturation wherein cells undergo structural changes both in their cell walls and protoplasm is termed differentiation.
False 1: The act leading to maturation wherein cells undergo structural changes both in their cell walls and protoplasm is termed dedifferentiation.

True Statement: To form a tracheary element, the cells lose their protoplasm and develop a strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell wall.
False 1: To form a tracheary element, the cells retain their protoplasm and develop a strong primary cell wall.

True Statement: Living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions – this phenomenon is termed dedifferentiation.
False 1: Living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions – this phenomenon is termed redifferentiation.

True Statement: Formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of dedifferentiation.
False 1: Formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of redifferentiation.

True Statement: Development is the sum of growth and differentiation.
False 1: Growth is the sum of development and differentiation.

True Statement: Development is a term that includes all changes that an organism goes through during its life cycle from germination of the seed to senescence.
False 1: Growth is a term that includes all changes that an organism goes through during its life cycle from germination of the seed to senescence.

True Statement: The ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures is called plasticity.
False 1: The ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures is called heterophylly.

True Statement: In cotton, coriander and larkspur, the leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants – this is called heterophylly.
False 1: In cotton, coriander and larkspur, the leaves of the juvenile plant are identical in shape to those in mature plants.

True Statement: Plant growth regulators (PGRs) are small, simple molecules of diverse chemical composition.
False 1: Plant growth regulators (PGRs) are large, complex molecules of uniform chemical composition.

True Statement: Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is an indole compound PGR.
False 1: Gibberellic acid (GA₃) is an indole compound PGR.

True Statement: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a derivative of carotenoids.
False 1: Gibberellic acid (GA₃) is a derivative of carotenoids.

True Statement: Gibberellic acid (GA₃) is a terpene.
False 1: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a terpene.

True Statement: Ethylene (C₂H₄) is a gaseous PGR.
False 1: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a gaseous PGR.

True Statement: Kinetin is an adenine derivative PGR.
False 1: Abscisic acid (ABA) is an adenine derivative PGR.

True Statement: Auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins are plant growth promoters involved in growth promoting activities.
False 1: Auxins, gibberellins and abscisic acid are plant growth promoters involved in growth promoting activities.

True Statement: Abscisic acid plays an important role in dormancy and abscission and is classified as a growth inhibitor.
False 1: Ethylene plays an important role in dormancy and abscission and is classified as a growth inhibitor.

True Statement: Ethylene is largely an inhibitor of growth activities.
False 1: Ethylene is largely a promoter of growth activities.

True Statement: Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed that coleoptiles of canary grass responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source (phototropism).
False 1: Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed that coleoptiles of oat seedlings responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source (phototropism).

True Statement: The tip of the coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile.
False 1: The base of the coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile.

True Statement: Auxin was isolated by F.W. Went from tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings.
False 1: Auxin was isolated by F.W. Went from tips of coleoptiles of canary grass seedlings.
False 2: Kinetin was isolated by F.W. Went from tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings.

True Statement: The 'bakanae' (foolish seedling) disease of rice seedlings was caused by a fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi.
False 1: The 'bakanae' (foolish seedling) disease of wheat seedlings was caused by a fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi.

True Statement: The active substances from Gibberella fujikuroi were later identified as gibberellic acid.
False 1: The active substances from Gibberella fujikuroi were later identified as auxins.

True Statement: H.H. Cousins (1910) confirmed the release of a volatile substance from ripened oranges that hastened the ripening of stored unripened bananas.
False 1: H.H. Cousins (1910) confirmed the release of a volatile substance from ripened bananas that hastened the ripening of stored unripened oranges.

True Statement: F. Skoog and co-workers observed that callus proliferated from tobacco stem internodal segments only if, in addition to auxins, the medium was supplemented with extracts of vascular tissues, yeast extract, coconut milk or DNA.
False 1: F. Skoog and co-workers observed that callus proliferated from rice stem internodal segments only if, in addition to auxins, the medium was supplemented with extracts of vascular tissues, yeast extract, coconut milk or DNA.

True Statement: Miller et al. (1955) identified and crystallised the cytokinesis-promoting active substance termed kinetin.
False 1: Miller et al. (1955) identified and crystallised the cytokinesis-promoting active substance termed zeatin.

True Statement: During mid-1960s, three independent researches reported the purification of three different inhibitors – inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin – that were later proven to be chemically identical and named abscisic acid (ABA).
False 1: During mid-1960s, three independent researches reported the purification of three different inhibitors – inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin – that were later proven to be chemically different.

True Statement: Cytokinins were discovered as kinetin (a modified form of adenine, a purine) from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA.
False 1: Auxins were discovered as kinetin (a modified form of adenine, a purine) from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

True Statement: Kinetin does not occur naturally in plants.
False 1: Kinetin occurs naturally in plants.

True Statement: Zeatin was isolated from corn-kernels and coconut milk as a natural cytokinin.
False 1: Kinetin was isolated from corn-kernels and coconut milk as a natural cytokinin.

True Statement: Natural cytokinins are synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs, for example, root apices, developing shoot buds, young fruits.
False 1: Natural cytokinins are synthesised in regions where cells are fully matured, for example, old leaves and bark.

True Statement: Auxins (from Greek 'auxein': to grow) were first isolated from human urine.
False 1: Cytokinins were first isolated from human urine.

True Statement: IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) and IBA (indole butyric acid) have been isolated from plants as natural auxins.
False 1: NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic) have been isolated from plants as natural auxins.

True Statement: NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic) are synthetic auxins.
False 1: IAA (indole-3-acetic acid) and IBA (indole butyric acid) are synthetic auxins.

True Statement: Auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, used widely for plant propagation.
False 1: Cytokinins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings, used widely for plant propagation.

True Statement: Auxins promote flowering in pineapples.
False 1: Gibberellins promote flowering in pineapples.

True Statement: Auxins help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.
False 1: Cytokinins help to prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote the abscission of older mature leaves and fruits.

True Statement: In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds – this phenomenon is called apical dominance.
False 1: In most higher plants, the growing lateral buds inhibit the growth of the apical bud – this phenomenon is called apical dominance.

True Statement: Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) usually results in the growth of lateral buds.
False 1: Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) usually results in inhibition of lateral buds.

True Statement: Auxins induce parthenocarpy, e.g., in tomatoes.
False 1: Gibberellins induce parthenocarpy, e.g., in tomatoes.

True Statement: 2,4-D is widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds and does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.
False 1: 2,4-D is widely used to kill monocotyledonous weeds and does not affect mature dicotyledonous plants.

True Statement: Auxin also controls xylem differentiation and helps in cell division.
False 1: Gibberellin also controls xylem differentiation and helps in cell division.

True Statement: There are more than 100 gibberellins reported from widely different organisms such as fungi and higher plants.
False 1: There are fewer than 10 gibberellins reported from widely different organisms such as fungi and higher plants.

True Statement: Gibberellic acid (GA₃) was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form.
False 1: GA₁ was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form.

True Statement: All GAs are acidic.
False 1: All GAs are basic (alkaline).

True Statement: The ability of gibberellins to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grape stalks.
False 1: The ability of auxins to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grape stalks.

True Statement: Gibberellins cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape.
False 1: Auxins cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape.

True Statement: Gibberellins delay senescence, allowing fruits to remain on the tree longer to extend the market period.
False 1: Ethylene delays senescence, allowing fruits to remain on the tree longer to extend the market period.
False 2: Gibberellins accelerate senescence, causing fruits to drop earlier.

True Statement: GA₃ is used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.
False 1: Ethylene is used to speed up the malting process in the brewing industry.

True Statement: Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.
False 1: Spraying sugarcane crop with auxins increases the length of the stem, increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.

True Statement: Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, leading to early seed production.
False 1: Spraying juvenile conifers with auxins hastens the maturity period, leading to early seed production.

True Statement: Gibberellins promote bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.
False 1: Cytokinins promote bolting in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.

True Statement: Cytokinins help produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation.
False 1: Auxins help produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation.

True Statement: Cytokinins help overcome apical dominance.
False 1: Auxins help overcome apical dominance.

True Statement: Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence.
False 1: Auxins promote nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence.

True Statement: Ethylene is synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits.
False 1: Auxin is synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits.

True Statement: Ethylene promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs especially of leaves and flowers.
False 1: Cytokinin promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs especially of leaves and flowers.

True Statement: Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening and enhances the respiration rate during ripening of fruits.
False 1: Gibberellin is highly effective in fruit ripening and enhances the respiration rate during ripening of fruits.

True Statement: The rise in rate of respiration during ripening of fruits is called respiratory climactic.
False 1: The rise in rate of respiration during ripening of fruits is called anaerobic respiration.

True Statement: Ethylene breaks seed and bud dormancy and initiates germination in peanut seeds and sprouting of potato tubers.
False 1: Abscisic acid breaks seed and bud dormancy and initiates germination in peanut seeds and sprouting of potato tubers.

True Statement: Ethylene promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants, helping leaves and upper parts of the shoot to remain above water.
False 1: Gibberellin promotes rapid internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice plants, helping leaves and upper parts of the shoot to remain above water.

True Statement: Ethylene promotes root growth and root hair formation, helping plants to increase their absorption surface.
False 1: Gibberellin promotes root growth and root hair formation, helping plants to increase their absorption surface.

True Statement: Ethylene is used to initiate flowering and synchronise fruit-set in pineapples.
False 1: Gibberellins are used to initiate flowering and synchronise fruit-set in pineapples.

True Statement: Ethylene also induces flowering in mango.
False 1: Gibberellins also induce flowering in mango.

True Statement: The most widely used compound as a source of ethylene is ethephon.
False 1: The most widely used compound as a source of gibberellin is ethephon.

True Statement: Ethephon hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples and accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits.
False 1: Abscisic acid hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples and accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits.

True Statement: Ethephon promotes female flowers in cucumbers thereby increasing the yield.
False 1: Ethephon promotes male flowers in cucumbers thereby decreasing the yield.

True Statement: Abscisic acid (ABA) was discovered for its role in regulating abscission and dormancy.
False 1: Ethylene was discovered for its role in regulating abscission and dormancy.

True Statement: ABA acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism.
False 1: Ethylene acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism.

True Statement: ABA inhibits seed germination.
False 1: Gibberellin inhibits seed germination.

True Statement: ABA stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses; therefore it is also called the stress hormone.
False 1: Ethylene stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses; therefore it is also called the stress hormone.

True Statement: ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy.
False 1: Gibberellin plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy.

True Statement: By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.
False 1: By inducing germination, gibberellin helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.

True Statement: In most situations, ABA acts as an antagonist to GAs.
False 1: In most situations, cytokinin acts as an antagonist to GAs.
